draft.title: Exponential models
card: An exponential model has the form y = a × b^t. The value a is the initial value, when t = 0. The base b is the growth or decay factor for each time step.
a rise of r% per time step has b = 1 + r/100. A rise of 5% gives b = 1.05. Here b is more than 1.
a fall of r% per time step has b = 1 − r/100. A fall of 20% gives b = 0.8. Here b is between 0 and 1.
Example: $200 grows 10% each year, so y = 200 × 1.1^t. After 2 years, y = 200 × 1.21 = $242. If a quantity doubles every 3 hours, then y = a × 2^(t/3).
draft.remember: y = a × b^t: a is the start, b is 1 plus the rate for growth, or 1 minus the rate for decay.

a.q: A town of 4000 people grows by 3% each year. Which rule gives its population P after t years?
a.why: Growth of 3% means the factor is 1 + 0.03 = 1.03, and the population is multiplied by it each year. Using 0.03 would shrink the population to almost nothing.
a.clue: Each year the population becomes 103% of the year before.

b.q: A drug in the blood has a half-life of 4 hours. Dose 80 mg is taken. How much remains after 12 hours?
b.why: 12 hours is 3 half-lives, so the amount is halved three times: 80 → 40 → 20 → 10 mg. Halving only once gives 40 mg, and dividing by 3 gives 26.7 mg.
b.clue: Count how many half-lives fit into 12 hours.

problems.detail: The question depends on half-life, but the card never explains it. It shows only a doubling-time example, even though half-life is part of this point. The card should show the half-life form, y = a × (1/2)^(t/h), or at least explain halving per half-life.
'b is 1 plus the rate' does not say the rate must be a decimal (r/100), as the card does. A student could read 5% growth as b = 1 + 5 = 6.

proposal.title: Exponential models
card: An exponential model has the form y = a × b^t. The value a is the initial value, when t = 0. The base b is the growth or decay factor for each time step.
For a rise of r% per step, b = 1 + r/100, so a 5% rise gives b = 1.05. For a fall of r%, b = 1 − r/100, so a 20% fall gives b = 0.8.
Example: $200 grows 10% each year, so y = 200 × 1.1^t. After 2 years, y = 200 × 1.21 = $242.
If a quantity doubles every d hours (its doubling time), y = a × 2^(t/d). If it halves every h hours (its half-life), y = a × (1/2)^(t/h).
proposal.remember: Start value a, then multiply by b each step: b = 1 + r/100 for growth, 1 − r/100 for decay.
